newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk police defy Yilmaz in journalist murder case.
newsitem.headline: Turk police defy Yilmaz in journalist murder case.

text.p: Five Turkish policemen on Thursday failed to turn up at a trial on their alleged involvement in the murder of a leftist journalist, despite Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz ordering them to appear in court.
Anatolian news agency said none of the 48 policemen charged in the beating death of journalist Metin Goktepe in 1996 appeared at the trial in the western town of Afyon.

Yilmaz phoned Interior Minister Murat Basesgioglu on Wednesday in the presence of journalists and told him to ensure that five policemen with arrest warrants against them in the case attended Thursday's hearing.
He acknowledged on Thursday that it was difficult to find the policemen because they had been suspended from duty and had gone on the run. He promised they would be brought to court.
"Starting on Monday, work will begin to bring these policemen to justice," he told a meeting of business leaders. He gave no further details.
The suspects, so far exempted from attending the trial, face sentences of between three and 15 years.
Goktepe was beaten to death while in police custody in January last year. He was one of scores of people rounded up for an identity check after the funerals of two far-left prisoners.
The case has been delayed after being transferred twice to different provinces for what officials said were security reasons.
Human rights activists say the moves were attempts to keep the case out of the public eye by delaying the trial.
Thursday's hearing was brief and the case was adjourned until August, NTV television news channel said.
